title: Writing Ingress Resources 📝
description: Create host, path rules, and secure your endpoints with TLS.

slides.title: The Anatomy of an Ingress YAML 🧬
slides.content:
# Four main sections

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: my-ingress
  annotations: {}
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  rules: [...]
  tls: [...]
```
- `rules`: array of host/path rules.
- `tls`: section for HTTPS secrets.

slides.title: Path‑Based Routing 🛤️
slides.content:
## Split traffic by URL path

```yaml
rules:
- host: shop.example.com
  http:
    paths:
    - path: /products
      pathType: Prefix
      backend:
        service:
          name: product-svc
          port:
            number: 80
    - path: /orders
      pathType: Prefix
      backend:
        service:
          name: order-svc
          port:
            number: 80
```

Requests to `shop.example.com/products/*` go to `product-svc`, `/orders/*` to `order-svc`.

slides.title: Apply the Ingress
slides.codeSnippet:
kubectl apply -f path-ingress.yaml
kubectl get ingress

quizData.question: What does `pathType: Prefix` mean?

options.text: Matches the path and any sub‑paths that start with it

quizData.explanation: Prefix matching routes `/foo` and `/foo/bar` to the same backend.

slides.title: Host‑Based Routing 🏨
slides.content:
## Different domains, different backends

```yaml
rules:
- host: api.example.com
  http:
    paths:
    - path: /
      pathType: Prefix
      backend:
        service:
          name: api-svc
          port:
            number: 80
- host: web.example.com
  http:
    paths:
    - path: /
      pathType: Prefix
      backend:
        service:
          name: web-svc
          port:
            number: 80
```

Allows virtual hosting on the same IP.

slides.title: Enabling TLS 🔐
slides.content:
## HTTPS with a TLS certificate

First, create a TLS Secret:
```bash
kubectl create secret tls my-tls-secret --cert=cert.pem --key=key.pem
```

Then reference it in the Ingress:
```yaml
tls:
- hosts:
  - example.com
  secretName: my-tls-secret
```

The Ingress controller will terminate TLS and forward decrypted traffic to Services.

slides.title: Ingress with TLS YAML
slides.codeSnippet:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: secure-ingress
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  tls:
  - hosts:
    - secure.example.com
    secretName: tls-secret
  rules:
  - host: secure.example.com
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: my-service
            port:
              number: 443

quizData.question: Where does TLS termination happen with an Ingress?
quizData.explanation: The controller decrypts TLS and forwards plain HTTP to the backend Service.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use cert‑manager for automatic TLS

cert‑manager can automatically provision and renew Let’s Encrypt certificates. Just add an annotation to your Ingress.
